key_insight: Critically damped Polyak (CDP) stepsizes adapt gradient descent to local curvature, promoting flatter minima while enabling convergence to an interpolating solution.
engineering_relevance: CDP offers an adaptive stepsize approach to reducing sharpness, with demonstrated flattening in nonlinear teacher–student networks and pretrained LLM fine-tuning.
method: Multiply the classical Polyak stepsize by 4 and a mild damping factor.
Use curvature-adaptive oscillations near the minimizer manifold, with damping driving convergence.
At low loss, induce motion along the manifold that approximately minimizes log top Hessian eigenvalue.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports uniform-in-time sharpness and loss-reduction guarantees for locally quadratic Morse–Bott losses, plus empirical flattening similar to SAM in settings beyond the theory.
watch_item: The guarantees require local Morse–Bott structure near the minimizer manifold; the reported LLM results extend beyond this theoretical scope.
paper_title: A new algorithmic approach for finding flat minima: critically damped Polyak stepsizes
